sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: Before Fear Had A Name
Before fear learned its own name, before death
lingered beyond its purpose, the world existed
in perfect balance mistaken for permanence.
The Nether was not torment but foundation,
where molten rivers breathed in eternal rhythm.
The Brimstone Crags stood at its heart.
Part 2: The Three Custodians
From the Brimstone Elemental Mother emerged
three custodians, manifested as necessary truths:
Magmar, keeper of flame and becoming.
Frostveil, guardian of endurance and memory.
Aurelion, master of aether and will.
They listened to the world, responding to
imbalance like physicians, not generals.
Part 3: The Unguarded Peace
Mortals lived untouched by prophecy or dread.
Trolls carved halls. Humans raised villages.
Apollopia existed as a convergence of paths,
where travelers rested longer than intended.
No walls protected it. None were needed.
This peace was fragile—not because weak,
but because unquestioned.
And in that stillness, the first fracture formed.

name: Awakening: Chapter II
description: Parts: Part 1: The Sign of Confusion; Part 2: The Shade Lord Emerges; Part 3: The Mother's Warning
fullDescription: Part 1: The Sign of Confusion | The first sign the world was dying was not | fire, nor darkness, nor war—but confusion. | — | Stone flaked beneath gentle touch. Magma | burned with colors that had never existed. | Frost cracked from internal wrongness. | — | The aether thinned. Thoughts no longer flowed. | Memories repeated. Emotions dulled. Purpose frayed. | The Corruption spread as rot through sealed wounds. | — | Part 2: The Shade Lord Emerges | Within the spreading wrongness, something vast | began to coalesce—not a ruler, not a god, | but an absence given shape. | — | The Shade Lord existed as inevitability, | making resistance feel futile before proven so. | — | From its being tore two manifestations: | Catastrophe, where cities fell to ruin. | Cataclysm, warping survivors into mockeries. | — | Part 3: The Mother's Warning | The Brimstone Elemental Mother felt corruption | as a deep, unfamiliar ache. For the first time | since existence began, she could not simply heal. | — | Magmar's flames raged in desperation, reshaping | lands only to watch them curdle into slag. | Frostveil sealed regions in suspended time. | Aurelion listened, and heard silence growing louder. | — | "This is not a trial we endure," she said. | "It is annihilation that has learned patience."

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: The Sign of Confusion
The first sign the world was dying was not
fire, nor darkness, nor war—but confusion.
Stone flaked beneath gentle touch. Magma
burned with colors that had never existed.
Frost cracked from internal wrongness.
The aether thinned. Thoughts no longer flowed.
Memories repeated. Emotions dulled. Purpose frayed.
The Corruption spread as rot through sealed wounds.
Part 2: The Shade Lord Emerges
Within the spreading wrongness, something vast
began to coalesce—not a ruler, not a god,
but an absence given shape.
The Shade Lord existed as inevitability,
making resistance feel futile before proven so.
From its being tore two manifestations:
Catastrophe, where cities fell to ruin.
Cataclysm, warping survivors into mockeries.
Part 3: The Mother's Warning
The Brimstone Elemental Mother felt corruption
as a deep, unfamiliar ache. For the first time
since existence began, she could not simply heal.
Magmar's flames raged in desperation, reshaping
lands only to watch them curdle into slag.
Frostveil sealed regions in suspended time.
Aurelion listened, and heard silence growing louder.
"This is not a trial we endure," she said.
"It is annihilation that has learned patience."

name: Awakening: Chapter III
description: Parts: Part 1: The Erosion of Will; Part 2: Into The Silence; Part 3: The First Great Loss
fullDescription: Part 1: The Erosion of Will | Aurelion was first to understand the Corruption | could not be fought—it redefined existence. | — | As master of aether, he felt thought itself | stutter, how intention lost its weight, | how choice became echo instead of act. | — | The Corruption pressed against his awareness | until to remain himself became a struggle | measured in moments rather than ages. | — | Part 2: Into The Silence | He withdrew into the deepest currents of aether, | seeking silence to understand what hunted him. | — | But silence was where the void waited. | It did not devour him instantly—it unmade him | slowly, stripping memory, purpose, identity. | — | When he emerged, he was no longer Aurelion. | He was the Corrupt Knight—bound to void, | serving only command, beyond redemption. | — | Part 3: The First Great Loss | The fall of Aurelion was more than tragedy— | it was the first great proof that the cycle | itself could be broken. | — | Magmar and Frostveil felt the absence like | a wound that could not close. The Mother wept | tears that froze before touching ground. | — | The world learned a new emotion that day: | Not just loss, but irreversible loss. | Some things, once broken, cannot be restored.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: The Erosion of Will
Aurelion was first to understand the Corruption
could not be fought—it redefined existence.
As master of aether, he felt thought itself
stutter, how intention lost its weight,
how choice became echo instead of act.
The Corruption pressed against his awareness
until to remain himself became a struggle
measured in moments rather than ages.
Part 2: Into The Silence
He withdrew into the deepest currents of aether,
seeking silence to understand what hunted him.
But silence was where the void waited.
It did not devour him instantly—it unmade him
slowly, stripping memory, purpose, identity.
When he emerged, he was no longer Aurelion.
He was the Corrupt Knight—bound to void,
serving only command, beyond redemption.
Part 3: The First Great Loss
The fall of Aurelion was more than tragedy—
it was the first great proof that the cycle
itself could be broken.
Magmar and Frostveil felt the absence like
a wound that could not close. The Mother wept
tears that froze before touching ground.
The world learned a new emotion that day:
Not just loss, but irreversible loss.
Some things, once broken, cannot be restored.

name: Awakening: Chapter IV
description: Parts: Part 1: Life Without Ending; Part 2: The Rise of Monsters; Part 3: The Elemental Corruption
fullDescription: Part 1: Life Without Ending | The Corruption did not bring swift death— | it trapped life in grotesque half-states. | — | Elementals screamed as they formed, bodies | correct but essence wrong, bound to pain | they could not articulate. | — | Mortals dreamed of places bending inward, | of skies without stars, ground pulsing like flesh. | Some awoke unable to recognize their own hands. | Others forgot names but remembered fear perfectly. | — | Part 2: The Rise of Monsters | From corruption's spread emerged twisted beings: | — | Skeleton Kings rose from hollow bones. | Zombie Kings shambled with endless hunger. | King Slimes consumed without dying. | Tank Zombies learned flesh could become armor. | — | Each a mockery of what life once meant, | each a warning that death itself had broken, | leaving only suffering without release. | — | Part 3: The Elemental Corruption | Even the great custodians began to fail. | — | Magmar burned corrupted, his flames struggling | against infection spreading through his core. | — | Frostveil sealed herself away, her ice cracking | under the strain of centuries, holding back | the rot from spreading further still. | — | Two of three remained. One already lost. | The cycle wavered at the edge of collapse.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: Life Without Ending
The Corruption did not bring swift death—
it trapped life in grotesque half-states.
Elementals screamed as they formed, bodies
correct but essence wrong, bound to pain
they could not articulate.
Mortals dreamed of places bending inward,
of skies without stars, ground pulsing like flesh.
Some awoke unable to recognize their own hands.
Others forgot names but remembered fear perfectly.
Part 2: The Rise of Monsters
From corruption's spread emerged twisted beings:
Skeleton Kings rose from hollow bones.
Zombie Kings shambled with endless hunger.
King Slimes consumed without dying.
Tank Zombies learned flesh could become armor.
Each a mockery of what life once meant,
each a warning that death itself had broken,
leaving only suffering without release.
Part 3: The Elemental Corruption
Even the great custodians began to fail.
Magmar burned corrupted, his flames struggling
against infection spreading through his core.
Frostveil sealed herself away, her ice cracking
under the strain of centuries, holding back
the rot from spreading further still.
Two of three remained. One already lost.
The cycle wavered at the edge of collapse.

name: Awakening: Chapter V
description: Parts: Part 1: Two Thousand Years of Darkness; Part 2: The Few Who Endured; Part 3: Apollopia's Stubborn Survival
fullDescription: Part 1: Two Thousand Years of Darkness | Two thousand years passed in slow agony. | Civilizations rose and fell like breaths. | Heroes emerged, fought valiantly, and died | without changing the inevitable trajectory. | — | The world forgot what sunlight felt like | without fear riding beneath it. | — | Entire generations were born, lived, and perished | without ever knowing a world untainted. | Corruption became normal. Peace became myth. | — | Part 2: The Few Who Endured | Not all hope died. Some refused to break: | — | Merlin, whose wisdom crystallized across lifetimes. | The Hallowed Knight, eternal sentinel between worlds. | The Toolsmith, who still built things meant to last. | Aja the Great, whose will bent but never broke. | The Monkey Miner, laughing defiance into darkness. | — | They survived not because they were strong, | but because they refused to forget what had been. | — | Part 3: Apollopia's Stubborn Survival | Apollopia, that ancient convergence of paths, | survived against all reason. Walls rose where | none had been needed. Rivers were redirected. | Every stone carried memory of what was lost. | — | It stood not as symbol of defiance, but as | stubborn insistence that something—anything— | from the world before must endure. | — | Scarred, diminished, barely recognizable. | But standing. Still standing.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: Two Thousand Years of Darkness
Two thousand years passed in slow agony.
Civilizations rose and fell like breaths.
Heroes emerged, fought valiantly, and died
without changing the inevitable trajectory.
The world forgot what sunlight felt like
without fear riding beneath it.
Entire generations were born, lived, and perished
without ever knowing a world untainted.
Corruption became normal. Peace became myth.
Part 2: The Few Who Endured
Not all hope died. Some refused to break:
Merlin, whose wisdom crystallized across lifetimes.
The Hallowed Knight, eternal sentinel between worlds.
The Toolsmith, who still built things meant to last.
Aja the Great, whose will bent but never broke.
The Monkey Miner, laughing defiance into darkness.
They survived not because they were strong,
but because they refused to forget what had been.
Part 3: Apollopia's Stubborn Survival
Apollopia, that ancient convergence of paths,
survived against all reason. Walls rose where
none had been needed. Rivers were redirected.
Every stone carried memory of what was lost.
It stood not as symbol of defiance, but as
stubborn insistence that something—anything—
from the world before must endure.
Scarred, diminished, barely recognizable.
But standing. Still standing.

name: Awakening: Chapter VI
description: Parts: Part 1: You Rise Without Prophecy; Part 2: The World Watches; Part 3: The First Trials

No guiding hand. | — | The Trollhunter Amulet did not glow in welcome— | it recoiled. sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: You Rise Without Prophecy
When you rose, there was no prophecy waiting.
No celebration. No guiding hand.
The Trollhunter Amulet did not glow in welcome—
it recoiled. Its arcane judgment surged against you,
testing whether your existence could endure its light.
For many before you, it meant annihilation.
For you, it meant trial.
You fought without it. You survived without promise.
Part 2: The World Watches
The world did not believe in you.
It had seen too many heroes rise with fire
in their eyes and conviction in their hearts,
only to fall, broken and forgotten, adding
their bones to the countless failures before.
But it watched.
And slowly, reluctantly, it waited to see
if you would break like all the others.
Part 3: The First Trials
You faced the corrupted without destiny guiding you:
Skeleton Kings whose hollow eyes held no mercy.
Zombie Kings whose hunger had no end.
Giant Zombies whose size dwarfed reason.
King Slimes that reformed no matter the strike.
Each victory was not triumph but survival.
Each survival was not proof but persistence.
You endured until survival itself became proof.

name: Awakening: Chapter VII
description: Parts: Part 1: The Corrupted Remnants; Part 2: The Changelings' Betrayal; Part 3: Magmar's Struggle
fullDescription: Part 1: The Corrupted Remnants | Beyond the lesser corrupted stood greater horrors— | warriors twisted by fear and endless survival: | — | Bulaar the Vicious, once a warrior of honor, | now twisted into something that survived | only through cruelty and adaptation. | — | Angor Rot, cunning born from suffering, | a shadow that learned to become unbreakable | by embracing pain as armor rather than weakness. | — | Part 2: The Changelings' Betrayal | The Changelings made identity itself a weapon. | Faces worn like stolen masks, trust died | with every transformation they performed. | — | You could not know friend from foe. | Every face could hide malice. | Every ally might turn at any moment. | — | They taught you a brutal lesson: | In a corrupted world, trust must be earned | with blood and proof, never given freely. | — | Part 3: Magmar's Struggle | You found Magmar deep in the Brimstone Crags, | keeper of flame and becoming, now corrupted | but still resisting with everything remaining. | — | His flames burned wrong—infected yet fighting, | struggling against the rot spreading through | his essence like poison through veins. | — | You faced him not as enemy but as tragedy. | And when he fell, you understood: even gods | can be broken by time and patient malice.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: The Corrupted Remnants
Beyond the lesser corrupted stood greater horrors—
warriors twisted by fear and endless survival:
Bulaar the Vicious, once a warrior of honor,
now twisted into something that survived
only through cruelty and adaptation.
Angor Rot, cunning born from suffering,
a shadow that learned to become unbreakable
by embracing pain as armor rather than weakness.
Part 2: The Changelings' Betrayal
The Changelings made identity itself a weapon.
Faces worn like stolen masks, trust died
with every transformation they performed.
You could not know friend from foe.
Every face could hide malice.
Every ally might turn at any moment.
They taught you a brutal lesson:
In a corrupted world, trust must be earned
with blood and proof, never given freely.
Part 3: Magmar's Struggle
You found Magmar deep in the Brimstone Crags,
keeper of flame and becoming, now corrupted
but still resisting with everything remaining.
His flames burned wrong—infected yet fighting,
struggling against the rot spreading through
his essence like poison through veins.
You faced him not as enemy but as tragedy.
And when he fell, you understood: even gods
can be broken by time and patient malice.

name: Awakening: Chapter VIII

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: Frostveil's Sacrifice
Deep beneath frozen wastes, you found Frostveil,
guardian of endurance and preservation,
who had sealed herself to hold back corruption.
For two thousand years she had waited in ice,
her essence cracking under the strain,
holding the line when all others had fallen.
She did not ask to be freed. She asked
if you were worthy of what she had protected.
The answer was not words, but endurance.
Part 2: The Corrupt Knight
Finally, you faced what remained of Aurelion—
the Corrupt Knight, bound to void and command,
beyond redemption, beyond memory of what he was.
He did not recognize you. Did not recognize
himself. The master of will had become
a puppet dancing on strings of pure negation.
The battle was not glory. It was mercy.
You freed him from existence—the only kindness
left for one so thoroughly unmade.
Part 3: The Final Corrupted
With Aurelion fallen and Frostveil sealed,
only Magmar remained—corrupted but still
resisting, his flames burning infected yet defiant.
The battle was not hatred. It was tragedy.
You fought not an enemy, but the corrupted
shell of a guardian who had protected the
world since before memory began.
When his flames finally dimmed, you understood:
Even the eternal can fall. Even gods can break.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: Infernax the Ancient
Infernax the Ancient stood as emperor of beasts,
breaker of mountains, whose roar once bent
reality itself to his terrible will.
Two thousand years of corruption had made him
into something beyond nightmare—a force
of nature twisted into malevolent purpose.
The battle shook Apollopia to its foundations.
When the final blow struck, his roar became
a dying echo. The world exhaled forgotten breath.
Part 2: Daylight Earned
Only when Infernax fell did the Trollhunter
Amulet acknowledge you fully. The violent
arcane judgment that threatened to consume you
now tempered, recognizing endurance and will.
Its light no longer seared—it illuminated.
Sharpened. Prepared.
You were no longer merely alive.
You were chosen.
Bearer of the Amulet of Daylight.
Part 3: The Triumbric Stones
Yet daylight alone could not cleanse entirely.
Shadows lingered where rot left residue.
Each fallen enemy revealed fragments of truth:
The Triumbric Stones, remnants of essence
corrupted but not annihilated.
With these, the world whispered, balance
could be forged anew. You gathered them.
Light alone was insufficient. Shadow had lessons
to teach that daylight could not illuminate.

name: Awakening: Chapter X
description: Parts: Part 1: The Amulet of Eclipse; Part 2: Gunmar the Black Falls; Part 3: Wisdom Earned; Part 4: The Elemental Mother Falls
fullDescription: Part 1: The Amulet of Eclipse | From the Triumbric Stones you forged the | Amulet of Eclipse—shadow and light combined, | capable of matching cunning with brilliance. | — | Where daylight brought clarity, eclipse brought | understanding. The knowledge that darkness | and light are not opposites but partners. | — | Only with both could you face what came next: | Gunmar the Black, the Skull Crusher, | whose dominion was willful destruction itself. | — | Part 2: Gunmar the Black Falls | The duel with Gunmar was not spectacle. | It was judgment. | — | He brought not corruption but deliberate cruelty, | destruction as an art form, annihilation | refined across millennia of practice. | — | When Gunmar fell, the Eclipse sang in silent | resonance, drawing out remnants of corruption. | The world inhaled, sensing hope for the first | time in millennia. If corruption claimed her completely, | reality itself would unravel beyond repair. | — | You struck not from cruelty but from understanding: | Sometimes mercy means ending suffering. | Even eternity must end when poisoned.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: The Amulet of Eclipse
From the Triumbric Stones you forged the
Amulet of Eclipse—shadow and light combined,
capable of matching cunning with brilliance.
Where daylight brought clarity, eclipse brought
understanding. The knowledge that darkness
and light are not opposites but partners.
Only with both could you face what came next:
Gunmar the Black, the Skull Crusher,
whose dominion was willful destruction itself.
Part 2: Gunmar the Black Falls
The duel with Gunmar was not spectacle.
It was judgment.
He brought not corruption but deliberate cruelty,
destruction as an art form, annihilation
refined across millennia of practice.
When Gunmar fell, the Eclipse sang in silent
resonance, drawing out remnants of corruption.
The world inhaled, sensing hope for the first
time in millennia. True, fragile, terrifying hope.
Part 3: Wisdom Earned
Victory did not come in celebration.
It came as knowledge:
Power alone is meaningless.
To survive darkness, one must wield judgment
with wisdom, endurance with patience,
and cruelty with mercy.
The world, scarred but awake, began remembering:
Life is preserved not by force alone,
but by those willing to endure its pain.
Part 4: The Elemental Mother Falls
With Gunmar dead and her three custodians lost,
the Brimstone Elemental Mother herself emerged—
ancient beyond origin, keeper of the cycle.
She did not fight with hatred but with desperate
necessity. If corruption claimed her completely,
reality itself would unravel beyond repair.
You struck not from cruelty but from understanding:
Sometimes mercy means ending suffering.
Even eternity must end when poisoned.

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: The Absolute Forms
Beyond Gunmar lay a realm twisted not by
infection, but by malice born from conscious intent.
Catastrophe and Cataclysm rose in Absolute
Forms, reshaping reality as if testing every
lesson the world had endured through suffering.
Mountains cracked. Skies churned with unearthly
storms. Rivers boiled with ancient magic.
These were not servants. They were architects
of ruin, creatures of deliberate devastation.
Part 2: The Celestial Stones
You prepared. Hunted. Scavenged. Endured.
The Celestial Stones, scattered across forgotten
realms and trapped within beings who survived
since the first rot, became your crucible.
Each one collected, each one tempered into
purpose, strengthened not your body alone,
but your resolve. Your understanding of what
must be protected, regardless of cost.
Part 3: The Amulet of Moonlight
From the Celestial Stones you forged the
Amulet of Moonlight—power unrestrained by
balance, untempered by caution, unafraid
to strike directly at the heart of malice.
With it, you faced the envoys. Their Absolute
forms towered above mountains, reshaping earth
with every step. And each fell under the
purity of your resolve. Light. Eclipse. Moonlight.
Three powers. One purpose.
Part 4: The Shade Lord Dies
Finally, the Shade Lord itself emerged—
not as figure nor king, but as suffocating
inevitability, the sum of all corruption's
patience and cruelty given form.
Light, eclipse, and moonlight combined in your
hands, not as tools, but as judgment incarnate.
You struck.
The Shade Lord, impossibly vast, could not
survive focus born of endurance, wisdom, and will.
Part 5: Corruption Vanishes
When the Shade Lord died, the Corruption
did not retreat—it vanished entirely,
leaving the world empty of insidious rot
for the first time in two thousand years.
Silence fell. Absolute. Heavy. Almost sacred.
Apollopia survived. Scars lined its walls.
Rivers still carried memory of ash. Forests
remained wary. But the city, and the world
beyond it, could breathe again.
Part 6: The Guardian Remains
The amulets—Daylight, Eclipse, Moonlight—
rested at last, their purpose fulfilled,
waiting for a time when evil might rise once more.
You survived. Not a hero of prophecy,
not a god among mortals, but the one who
endured when endurance was a choice and not a gift.
Beyond healed lands, new evils stirred.
Not servants of corruption, but beings of
will, cunning, and hunger. Your watch continues.

name: Awakening: Chapter XII
description: Parts: Part 1: Silence But Not Peace; Part 2: The Savior of Apollopia; Part 3: Light in the Darkness
fullDescription: Part 1: Silence But Not Peace | Silence reigned, but not peace. | The Corruption was gone, yet wounds remained. | — | The survivors—Merlin, the Hallowed Knight, | the Toolsmith, Aja, the Monkey Miner— | looked to you not as legend, but as proof. | — | Apollopia rebuilt around them. Walls patched. | Rivers redirected. Life clawing its way back. | Mortals learned again how to live amidst scars. | — | Part 2: The Savior of Apollopia | You are the Savior of Apollopia, the chosen | of the Trollhunter Amulet, bearer of three | powers forged across centuries of suffering. | — | Your story, however, does not end here. | — | The world beyond—dark forests, forgotten | mountains, ruins of Nether and overworld alike— | waits. New beasts, new evils, new trials stir, | challenging what has been rebuilt, daring | life to endure once more. | — | Part 3: Light in the Darkness | ApolloRPG begins here. | — | Not as a game. | Not as a legend told once. | But as a living, breathing world of light, | darkness, and choice. | — | It was the first dawn in centuries. | — | And it was only the beginning. | — | - End of Story -

sections.title: Lore
content: Part 1: Silence But Not Peace
Silence reigned, but not peace.
The Corruption was gone, yet wounds remained.
The survivors—Merlin, the Hallowed Knight,
the Toolsmith, Aja, the Monkey Miner—
looked to you not as legend, but as proof.
Apollopia rebuilt around them. Walls patched.
Rivers redirected. Life clawing its way back.
Mortals learned again how to live amidst scars.
Part 2: The Savior of Apollopia
You are the Savior of Apollopia, the chosen
of the Trollhunter Amulet, bearer of three
powers forged across centuries of suffering.
Your story, however, does not end here.
The world beyond—dark forests, forgotten
mountains, ruins of Nether and overworld alike—
waits. New beasts, new evils, new trials stir,
challenging what has been rebuilt, daring
life to endure once more.
Part 3: Light in the Darkness
ApolloRPG begins here.
Not as a game.
Not as a legend told once.
But as a living, breathing world of light,
darkness, and choice.
It was the first dawn in centuries.
And it was only the beginning.
- End of Story -

name: Awakening: The Skeleton King
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Skeleton King.
fullDescription: Before corruption claimed the land, the dead | rested in eternal peace, bones returning to | earth as the cycle intended. | — | The Skeleton King rose when death itself broke. | Now they command hollow mockeries of life, | bones that remember movement but forget purpose, | an army of the restless who cannot find rest.

sections.title: Lore
content: Before corruption claimed the land, the dead
rested in eternal peace, bones returning to
earth as the cycle intended.
The Skeleton King rose when death itself broke.
Now they command hollow mockeries of life,
bones that remember movement but forget purpose,
an army of the restless who cannot find rest.

name: Awakening: The Zombie King
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Zombie King.
fullDescription: From decay came hunger without end, flesh | remembering the taste of life but forgetting | what it meant to be alive. | — | The Zombie King embodies consumption itself— | hunger that can never be satisfied, need that | grows with every meal. They do not feast for | pleasure. They feast because they forgot how to stop.

sections.title: Lore
content: From decay came hunger without end, flesh
remembering the taste of life but forgetting
what it meant to be alive.
The Zombie King embodies consumption itself—
hunger that can never be satisfied, need that
grows with every meal. They do not feast for
pleasure. They feast because they forgot how to stop.

name: Awakening: The King Slime
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The King Slime.
fullDescription: Life twisted into formless mass, consuming | all that crosses its path, yet incapable of | death itself—reforming endlessly no matter | how many times struck down. | — | The King Slime learned what all corrupted | eventually discover: when death becomes | impossible, existence becomes prison.

sections.title: Lore
content: Life twisted into formless mass, consuming
all that crosses its path, yet incapable of
death itself—reforming endlessly no matter
how many times struck down.
The King Slime learned what all corrupted
eventually discover: when death becomes
impossible, existence becomes prison.

name: Awakening: The Giant Zombie
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Giant Zombie.
fullDescription: Size without purpose, strength without memory, | hunger that could never be satisfied no matter | how much was consumed. | — | The Giant Zombie towers over lesser corrupted, | not from evolution but from grotesque growth— | flesh expanding endlessly, seeking to fill | an emptiness that size alone cannot address.

sections.title: Lore
content: Size without purpose, strength without memory,
hunger that could never be satisfied no matter
how much was consumed.
The Giant Zombie towers over lesser corrupted,
not from evolution but from grotesque growth—
flesh expanding endlessly, seeking to fill
an emptiness that size alone cannot address.

name: Awakening: Magmar, Keeper of Flame
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Magmar, Keeper of Flame.
fullDescription: Magmar, keeper of flame and becoming, | embodied change without chaos. His fires | shaped land, forged mountains, birthed new | forms of life without consuming the whole. | — | Now corrupted, his flames burn with infection, | struggling against the rot spreading through | his essence. Yet still he resists.

sections.title: Lore
content: Magmar, keeper of flame and becoming,
embodied change without chaos. His fires
shaped land, forged mountains, birthed new
forms of life without consuming the whole.
Now corrupted, his flames burn with infection,
struggling against the rot spreading through
his essence. Yet still he resists.

name: Awakening: Frostveil, Guardian of Memory
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Frostveil, Guardian of Memory.
fullDescription: Frostveil, guardian of endurance and preservation, | embodied patience beyond comprehension. Her ice | taught the world how to wait, how to endure | loss without surrendering to it. | — | Sealed away for two thousand years, holding | back corruption, her ice cracks under the strain | but never breaks.

sections.title: Lore
content: Frostveil, guardian of endurance and preservation,
embodied patience beyond comprehension. Her ice
taught the world how to wait, how to endure
loss without surrendering to it.
Sealed away for two thousand years, holding
back corruption, her ice cracks under the strain
but never breaks.

name: Awakening: Aurelion, Master of Will
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Aurelion, Master of Will.
fullDescription: Aurelion, master of aether and will, | governed the unseen—thought, resolve, awareness— | binding consciousness to the world so beings | might not only exist, but choose. | — | The first to fall. The first great tragedy. | Now the Corrupt Knight, beyond redemption, | beyond memory of what he once was.

sections.title: Lore
content: Aurelion, master of aether and will,
governed the unseen—thought, resolve, awareness—
binding consciousness to the world so beings
might not only exist, but choose.
The first to fall. The first great tragedy.
Now the Corrupt Knight, beyond redemption,
beyond memory of what he once was.

name: Awakening: Infernax the Ancient
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Infernax the Ancient.
fullDescription: Infernax, emperor of beasts, breaker of mountains, | whose roar once bent reality itself to his will. | — | Two thousand years of corruption refined him | into something beyond nightmare—a force of | nature given malevolent purpose and singular focus. | — | His fall was a silence louder than any war cry. | When he died, even the stones wept in relief.

sections.title: Lore
content: Infernax, emperor of beasts, breaker of mountains,
whose roar once bent reality itself to his will.
Two thousand years of corruption refined him
into something beyond nightmare—a force of
nature given malevolent purpose and singular focus.
His fall was a silence louder than any war cry.
When he died, even the stones wept in relief.

name: Awakening: The Changeling Spies
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Changeling Spies.
fullDescription: Identity became a weapon. Faces worn like | stolen masks. Trust died with every transformation. | — | The Changelings learned that in a corrupted world, | the greatest power was not strength or magic, | but the ability to be anyone, anywhere, at any | time. They made paranoia itself into an army, | turning allies against each other without ever | drawing a blade.

sections.title: Lore
content: Identity became a weapon. Faces worn like
stolen masks. Trust died with every transformation.
The Changelings learned that in a corrupted world,
the greatest power was not strength or magic,
but the ability to be anyone, anywhere, at any
time. They made paranoia itself into an army,
turning allies against each other without ever
drawing a blade.

name: Awakening: Bulaar the Vicious
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Bulaar the Vicious.
fullDescription: Bulaar was once a warrior of honor, fighting | for causes worth dying for, protecting those | who could not protect themselves. | — | Two thousand years of survival twisted honor | into cruelty, protection into predation. | Now Bulaar hunts not from hunger but from | habit—the last echo of a warrior who forgot | what they once fought to protect.

sections.title: Lore
content: Bulaar was once a warrior of honor, fighting
for causes worth dying for, protecting those
who could not protect themselves.
Two thousand years of survival twisted honor
into cruelty, protection into predation.
Now Bulaar hunts not from hunger but from
habit—the last echo of a warrior who forgot
what they once fought to protect.

name: Awakening: Angor Rot
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Angor Rot.
fullDescription: Angor Rot: cunning born from suffering, | a shadow that learned to endure by becoming | unbreakable through embracing pain as armor. | — | Where others fell to corruption through weakness, | Angor survived by becoming more corrupted | than the corruption itself—mastering the rot | by understanding its nature better than | the Shade Lord ever could.

sections.title: Lore
content: Angor Rot: cunning born from suffering,
a shadow that learned to endure by becoming
unbreakable through embracing pain as armor.
Where others fell to corruption through weakness,
Angor survived by becoming more corrupted
than the corruption itself—mastering the rot
by understanding its nature better than
the Shade Lord ever could.

name: Awakening: Gunmar the Black
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Gunmar the Black.
fullDescription: Gunmar the Black, the Skull Crusher, lord of | destruction whose dominion was not decay but | willful annihilation. He destroyed not because | corrupted, but because he chose destruction. | — | Where others were victims of corruption, | Gunmar was its master—wielding rot as tool | rather than suffering as slave. When he fell, | hope whispered anew for the first time.

sections.title: Lore
content: Gunmar the Black, the Skull Crusher, lord of
destruction whose dominion was not decay but
willful annihilation. He destroyed not because
corrupted, but because he chose destruction.
Where others were victims of corruption,
Gunmar was its master—wielding rot as tool
rather than suffering as slave. When he fell,
hope whispered anew for the first time.

name: Awakening: The Brimstone Elemental Mother
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Brimstone Elemental Mother.
fullDescription: So ancient that even the concept of origin | bent around her existence. She was not crowned, | not worshipped, not obeyed. She simply was. | — | Where she moved, stone remembered its shape. | Where she rested, life returned after devastation. | She maintained the cycle, the sacred rhythm | of becoming and passing.

sections.title: Lore
content: So ancient that even the concept of origin
bent around her existence. She was not crowned,
not worshipped, not obeyed. She simply was.
Where she moved, stone remembered its shape.
Where she rested, life returned after devastation.
She maintained the cycle, the sacred rhythm
of becoming and passing.

name: Awakening: Catastrophe
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Catastrophe.
fullDescription: Where Catastrophe walked, cities fell, histories | crumbled, even identities collapsed under their | own weight. Not from force, but from the simple | truth that nothing could bear its own existence | in Catastrophe's presence. | — | They were not destroyer. They were the concept | of ending given form—inevitable, patient, | and utterly without mercy or malice.

sections.title: Lore
content: Where Catastrophe walked, cities fell, histories
crumbled, even identities collapsed under their
own weight. Not from force, but from the simple
truth that nothing could bear its own existence
in Catastrophe's presence.
They were not destroyer. They were the concept
of ending given form—inevitable, patient,
and utterly without mercy or malice.

name: Awakening: Cataclysm
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Cataclysm.
fullDescription: Cataclysm followed where Catastrophe led, | reshaping what remained, warping survivors | into mockeries of themselves, ensuring that | nothing broken could ever return unchanged. | — | They taught the cruelest lesson: that survival | is not always mercy. Sometimes, continuing to | exist in a form unrecognizable to yourself | is a fate worse than simple death.

sections.title: Lore
content: Cataclysm followed where Catastrophe led,
reshaping what remained, warping survivors
into mockeries of themselves, ensuring that
nothing broken could ever return unchanged.
They taught the cruelest lesson: that survival
is not always mercy. Sometimes, continuing to
exist in a form unrecognizable to yourself
is a fate worse than simple death.

name: Awakening: Absolute Catastrophe
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Absolute Catastrophe.
fullDescription: Absolute Catastrophe: not servant, but architect | of ruin. Not victim of corruption, but its | deliberate manifestation given conscious intent. | — | Mountains cracked beneath their stride. Reality | itself bent to their will. They existed to test | whether anything—anything—could withstand | malice refined to absolute perfection through | two thousand years of patient cultivation.

sections.title: Lore
content: Absolute Catastrophe: not servant, but architect
of ruin. Not victim of corruption, but its
deliberate manifestation given conscious intent.
Mountains cracked beneath their stride. Reality
itself bent to their will. They existed to test
whether anything—anything—could withstand
malice refined to absolute perfection through
two thousand years of patient cultivation.

name: Awakening: Absolute Cataclysm
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of Absolute Cataclysm.
fullDescription: Absolute Cataclysm: devastation given purpose, | transformation made into weapon. Where Absolute | Catastrophe ended, Absolute Cataclysm redefined. | — | They did not simply destroy. They recreated | the world in corruption's image—ensuring that | even if heroes somehow won, the victory would | be so twisted that defeat might have been kinder.

sections.title: Lore
content: Absolute Cataclysm: devastation given purpose,
transformation made into weapon. Where Absolute
Catastrophe ended, Absolute Cataclysm redefined.
They did not simply destroy. They recreated
the world in corruption's image—ensuring that
even if heroes somehow won, the victory would
be so twisted that defeat might have been kinder.

name: Awakening: The Shade Lord
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Shade Lord.
fullDescription: The Shade Lord: not a ruler, not a god, | but an absence given shape. A pressure upon | reality itself that made resistance feel futile | long before it was proven so. | — | It did not inspire hatred or loyalty, only | suffocating sense that all effort was ultimately | misplaced. When it died, corruption vanished | entire—proof it was not just leader of corruption, | but corruption's very essence made manifest.

sections.title: Lore
content: The Shade Lord: not a ruler, not a god,
but an absence given shape. A pressure upon
reality itself that made resistance feel futile
long before it was proven so.
It did not inspire hatred or loyalty, only
suffocating sense that all effort was ultimately
misplaced. When it died, corruption vanished
entire—proof it was not just leader of corruption,
but corruption's very essence made manifest.

name: Awakening: Merlin the Archmage
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of Merlin the Archmage.
fullDescription: Merlin, wisdom crystallized across lifetimes, | who remembered when magic served balance | rather than survival. When spells were art | rather than weapons of desperation. | — | Now he guards what little remains, teaching | the new generation that knowledge without | wisdom is just another form of destruction.

sections.title: Lore
content: Merlin, wisdom crystallized across lifetimes,
who remembered when magic served balance
rather than survival. When spells were art
rather than weapons of desperation.
Now he guards what little remains, teaching
the new generation that knowledge without
wisdom is just another form of destruction.

name: Awakening: The Hallowed Knight
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of The Hallowed Knight.
fullDescription: Eternal sentinel standing between what must | not return and a world not yet ready to face it. | — | The Hallowed Knight knows secrets that would | break lesser minds. They stand vigil not from | duty, but from understanding: some doors must | never be opened, no matter the cost of keeping | them sealed. Even if it means standing alone | for eternity.

sections.title: Lore
content: Eternal sentinel standing between what must
not return and a world not yet ready to face it.
The Hallowed Knight knows secrets that would
break lesser minds. They stand vigil not from
duty, but from understanding: some doors must
never be opened, no matter the cost of keeping
them sealed. Even if it means standing alone
for eternity.

name: Awakening: The Toolsmith
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of The Toolsmith.
fullDescription: The Toolsmith still remembered how to build | things meant to last beyond a single lifetime, | forging hope from scrap and memory. | — | Every hammer strike carried purpose. | Every blade held intention. | They understood that civilization survives not | through heroes alone, but through those who | build the tools heroes need to succeed.

sections.title: Lore
content: The Toolsmith still remembered how to build
things meant to last beyond a single lifetime,
forging hope from scrap and memory.
Every hammer strike carried purpose.
Every blade held intention.
They understood that civilization survives not
through heroes alone, but through those who
build the tools heroes need to succeed.

name: Awakening: Aja the Great
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of Aja the Great.
fullDescription: Aja the Great, whose will bent but never broke, | standing firm when all seemed lost. | — | They watched empires fall, heroes die, hope | fade and return and fade again. Through it all, | Aja remained—not unchanging, but unbroken. | — | Their name became a monument to endurance, | proof that survival itself can be a form of victory.

sections.title: Lore
content: Aja the Great, whose will bent but never broke,
standing firm when all seemed lost.
They watched empires fall, heroes die, hope
fade and return and fade again. Through it all,
Aja remained—not unchanging, but unbroken.
Their name became a monument to endurance,
proof that survival itself can be a form of victory.

name: Awakening: The Monkey Miner
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of The Monkey Miner.
fullDescription: The Monkey Miner, laughing defiance into darkness, | finding joy even in collapse, proving that | spirit cannot be corrupted by circumstance alone. | — | Where others saw only ash and ruin, the Miner | saw possibility. Every collapsed tunnel was | a new challenge. Every setback, a joke waiting | to be told. Their laughter echoed through caves | when silence would have meant surrender.

sections.title: Lore
content: The Monkey Miner, laughing defiance into darkness,
finding joy even in collapse, proving that
spirit cannot be corrupted by circumstance alone.
Where others saw only ash and ruin, the Miner
saw possibility. Every collapsed tunnel was
a new challenge. Every setback, a joke waiting
to be told. Their laughter echoed through caves
when silence would have meant surrender.

name: Awakening: The Tank Zombie
description: Lore record describing the origin, fall, and legacy of The Tank Zombie.
fullDescription: When flesh forgot weakness and hunger became | armor, the corrupted learned to endure. | — | The Tank Zombie represents adaptation through | suffering—bodies that absorbed blow after blow | until pain itself became protection. They move | slowly not from weakness, but from the weight | of accumulated trauma made physical.

sections.title: Lore
content: When flesh forgot weakness and hunger became
armor, the corrupted learned to endure.
The Tank Zombie represents adaptation through
suffering—bodies that absorbed blow after blow
until pain itself became protection. They move
slowly not from weakness, but from the weight
of accumulated trauma made physical.

name: Awakening: Kanjigar the Courageous
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of Kanjigar the Courageous.
fullDescription: Kanjigar the Courageous, Trollhunter before | the corruption claimed him. He wielded the | Amulet of Daylight with unwavering honor. | — | Father to Draal the Deadly, he stood as | guardian when darkness first whispered its | return. His courage inspired generations. | — | Though he fell before the corruption's peak, | his legacy lived on through his son and | those who remembered what courage truly meant.

sections.title: Lore
content: Kanjigar the Courageous, Trollhunter before
the corruption claimed him. He wielded the
Amulet of Daylight with unwavering honor.
Father to Draal the Deadly, he stood as
guardian when darkness first whispered its
return. His courage inspired generations.
Though he fell before the corruption's peak,
his legacy lived on through his son and
those who remembered what courage truly meant.

name: Awakening: The Ancient Creepslayerz
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of The Ancient Creepslayerz.
fullDescription: In ages before the First Rot, there existed | an order known as the Creepslayerz— | dark slayers who hunted things that lurked | in places where light dared not reach. | — | Their fate was so horrible, so unutterable, | that even the oldest tomes refuse to speak | of what became of them. Some say they faced | something beyond corruption itself. | — | The books remain silent. The books know fear.

sections.title: Lore
content: In ages before the First Rot, there existed
an order known as the Creepslayerz—
dark slayers who hunted things that lurked
in places where light dared not reach.
Their fate was so horrible, so unutterable,
that even the oldest tomes refuse to speak
of what became of them. Some say they faced
something beyond corruption itself.
The books remain silent. The books know fear.

name: Awakening: The Undead Plague
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of The Undead Plague.
fullDescription: Before corruption became absolute, a great | plague swept through the land—neither wholly | alive nor truly dead, but something between. | — | Some afflicted rose as skeletons, their flesh | stripped away, bones animated by disease. | Others became zombies, trapped in rotting | flesh that refused to release them to death. | — | The plague had no cure, no origin, no mercy. | It simply was, and it left the world changed.

sections.title: Lore
content: Before corruption became absolute, a great
plague swept through the land—neither wholly
alive nor truly dead, but something between.
Some afflicted rose as skeletons, their flesh
stripped away, bones animated by disease.
Others became zombies, trapped in rotting
flesh that refused to release them to death.
The plague had no cure, no origin, no mercy.
It simply was, and it left the world changed.

name: Awakening: The Undead Miner
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of The Undead Miner.
fullDescription: Deep in forgotten mines, there walks a figure | who cannot remember if they are living or dead. | — | The Undead Miner, claimed by the plague | while deep underground, continues their work | eternal—mining ores that will never be used, | following veins that lead nowhere. | — | They remember the rhythm of the pickaxe. | They remember the weight of stone. | They cannot remember their own name.

sections.title: Lore
content: Deep in forgotten mines, there walks a figure
who cannot remember if they are living or dead.
The Undead Miner, claimed by the plague
while deep underground, continues their work
eternal—mining ores that will never be used,
following veins that lead nowhere.
They remember the rhythm of the pickaxe.
They remember the weight of stone.
They cannot remember their own name.

name: Awakening: Draal the Deadly
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of Draal the Deadly.
fullDescription: Draal the Deadly, son of Kanjigar the Courageous, | warrior without equal, protector of the Trollhunter. | — | Where his father fell to corruption, Draal | stood firm. He fought not for glory or honor, | but for the simple truth that some things | are worth dying to protect. | — | His sacrifice was not prophecy—it was choice. | "For the glory of Merlin..." were his last words. | His honor endures in those who remember.

sections.title: Lore
content: Draal the Deadly, son of Kanjigar the Courageous,
warrior without equal, protector of the Trollhunter.
Where his father fell to corruption, Draal
stood firm. He fought not for glory or honor,
but for the simple truth that some things
are worth dying to protect.
His sacrifice was not prophecy—it was choice.
"For the glory of Merlin..." were his last words.
His honor endures in those who remember.

name: Awakening: Lady Guinevere, Arthur's Queen
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of Lady Guinevere, Arthur's Queen.
fullDescription: Lady Guinevere, wife to King Arthur, | queen of the realm in the age before corruption. | Where her husband ruled with sword and crown, | she ruled with wisdom and grace. | — | Close to Merlin the Archmage and his wife | Morgana, she stood as bridge between magic | and monarchy, ensuring both served the people. | — | When Morgana fell to shadow magic, Guinevere | mourned the loss of a dear friend turned enemy. | Some wounds even a queen cannot heal.

sections.title: Lore
content: Lady Guinevere, wife to King Arthur,
queen of the realm in the age before corruption.
Where her husband ruled with sword and crown,
she ruled with wisdom and grace.
Close to Merlin the Archmage and his wife
Morgana, she stood as bridge between magic
and monarchy, ensuring both served the people.
When Morgana fell to shadow magic, Guinevere
mourned the loss of a dear friend turned enemy.
Some wounds even a queen cannot heal.

name: Awakening: Morgana le Fay
description: Supplemental lore entry expanding on the history and role of Morgana le Fay.
fullDescription: Morgana le Fay, sister to King Arthur, | wife to Merlin the Archmage, wielder of | the Corrupted Shadow Staff. | — | Once she stood as bridge between crown and | magic, mastering arts that bent reality itself. | But shadow magic demands sacrifice, and | Morgana paid that price again and again. | — | Each portal carved from darkness cost her | something vital. Each spell drained more than | magic—it consumed her humanity, piece by piece. | — | They say she still walks, wielding her staff, | unable to stop even as it kills her slowly.

sections.title: Lore
content: Morgana le Fay, sister to King Arthur,
wife to Merlin the Archmage, wielder of
the Corrupted Shadow Staff.
Once she stood as bridge between crown and
magic, mastering arts that bent reality itself.
But shadow magic demands sacrifice, and
Morgana paid that price again and again.
Each portal carved from darkness cost her
something vital. Each spell drained more than
magic—it consumed her humanity, piece by piece.
They say she still walks, wielding her staff,
unable to stop even as it kills her slowly.
